content:
If you've just bought a new Mac, like the recently launched Mac mini or Mac Studio, you might be thinking about picking up a new external monitor as well.

Here are my recommendations, covering multiple product categories, price points, and more options.

The Best External Monitors for Mac

Apple Studio Display

When it comes to the best monitors on the market, you absolutely can't leave out Apple's Studio Display. Although it's priced on the high end, it features Apple's signature sleek design and comes with a 27-inch 5K display.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K Retina display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 pixels per inch
  • Brightness: 600 nits
  • Color Support: Wide color gamut (P3), support for 1 billion colors
  • Refresh Rate: 60Hz
  • Camera: 12-megapixel Center Stage camera with Desk View support
  • True Tone Technology: Automatically adjusts the display's color temperature to match ambient lighting
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 5 ports (up to 120Gb/s) and two USB-C ports (up to 10Gb/s)
  • Host Charging: Up to 96W

The Studio Display comes in multiple configurations at different price points, which I've listed below. If you want an iMac-like experience, the Apple Studio Display is the obvious choice.

Standard glass with tilt-adjustable stand

Standard glass with tilt- and height-adjustable stand

Nano-texture glass with tilt-adjustable stand

Nano-texture glass with tilt- and height-adjustable stand

Apple Studio Display XDR

The Studio Display XDR launched earlier this year and outclasses the standard Studio Display in several ways, including mini-LED display technology and a 120Hz refresh rate.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K Retina XDR display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 pixels per inch, with mini-LED backlighting and 2,304 local dimming zones
  • Brightness: Up to 1,000 nits SDR, up to 2,000 nits HDR peak
  • Color Support: P3 and Adobe RGB wide color gamut, support for 1 billion colors
  • Refresh Rate: 120Hz with Adaptive Sync
  • Host Charging: Up to 140W

Of course, these advantages come at a higher price—even more expensive than the standard Studio Display.

Samsung M9 Smart Monitor

The 32-inch Samsung M9 Smart Monitor features a 4K OLED panel, making it a very appealing option for Mac users. My 9to5Toys colleague Justin Kahn switched to this monitor and said, "I've been pairing it with my Mac mini for a few months now and it's been fantastic."

  • Panel: 32-inch 4K OLED display (3840×2160 resolution) with anti-glare coating
  • Refresh Rate: 165Hz
  • Ports: DisplayPort, HDMI, USB-C, 2× USB-A
  • Built-in Camera: Yes, 4K
  • HDR Support: Yes (HDR10/HDR10+)

While it doesn't offer the 5K or 6K resolution of some other options on this list, you get the benefits of OLED, including deeper blacks, better color reproduction, and superior contrast.

LG UltraFine 6K

The LG UltraFine 6K represents LG's evolution in the high-end monitor market. It features a 32-inch panel with a resolution of 6144 x 3456 pixels and comes with multiple ports. Here are the key specs:

  • Display: 31.5-inch 6K Nano IPS Black display (6144×3456 resolution), 224 pixels per inch
  • Brightness: 450 nits typical; VESA DisplayHDR 600 certified
  • Color Support: 98% DCI-P3 and 99.5% Adobe RGB, support for 1.07 billion colors (10-bit)
  • Refresh Rate: 60Hz
  • Camera: None
  • True Tone Technology: None; supports auto-brightness adjustment
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 5 ports, one DisplayPort 2.1, one HDMI 2.1, two downstream USB-C ports, and one upstream USB-C port
  • Host Charging: Up to 96W via Thunderbolt
  • Contrast Ratio: 2,000:1

Click here to buy the LG UltraFine 6K

Asus ProArt 5K Display

My colleague Jeff Benjamin got hands-on with this monitor, and it immediately caught my attention. The Asus ProArt (PA27JCV) 5K display offers the same 5K resolution (5120×2880) as the Studio Display, also in a 27-inch size, but at half the price.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K IPS display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 pixels per inch
  • Brightness: 400 nits typical; VESA DisplayHDR 500 certified
  • Color Support: 99% DCI-P3, 100% sRGB, and 95% Adobe RGB, support for 1.07 billion colors (10-bit)
  • Refresh Rate: 60Hz with Adaptive-Sync
  • Camera: None
  • Ambient Light Adjustment: Ambient light and backlight sensors automatically adjust brightness and color temperature
  • Ports: One USB-C with DisplayPort Alt Mode, one DisplayPort 1.4, one HDMI 2.1, three USB-A, one downstream USB-C, and a headphone jack
  • Host Charging: Up to 96W via USB-C

Check out Jeff's full review for all the details. If you're looking for a 5K display to pair with your Mac, the Asus ProArt is hard to beat.

Click here to buy the Asus ProArt Display 5K:

Asus ProArt 6K Display

If you want a larger display with higher resolution, Asus has you covered too. The new Asus ProArt Display 6K (PA32QCV) is a 32-inch monitor with a native resolution of 6016 x 3384. Jeff called it "absurdly good value" in his review.

  • Display: 31.5-inch 6K IPS display (6016×3384 resolution), 218 pixels per inch
  • Brightness: 400 nits typical, 600 nits HDR peak; VESA DisplayHDR 600 certified
  • Color Support: 98% DCI-P3 and 100% sRGB, support for 1.07 billion colors (10-bit)
  • Refresh Rate: 60Hz with Adaptive-Sync (48–60Hz)
  • Camera: None
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 4 ports, one DisplayPort 1.4, one HDMI 2.1, USB-C and USB-A hub functionality, and a headphone jack
  • Host Charging: Up to 96W via Thunderbolt 4

The biggest selling point of the ASUS ProArt 6K Display might be its price. It's significantly cheaper than some of the most popular 4K and 5K monitors on the market.

Samsung ViewFinity S8 5K (S80HF)

Samsung's ViewFinity S8 5K is another very attractive option to pair with your new Mac, offering 5K resolution.

  • Brightness: 350 nits typical
  • Color Support: 99% sRGB, support for 1.07 billion colors; HDR10
  • Refresh Rate: 60Hz
  • Camera: None
  • Ambient Light Adjustment: Adaptive Picture automatically adjusts brightness based on ambient lighting
  • Ports: One USB-C port with 90W power delivery, one HDMI 2.1, one DisplayPort 1.4, three USB-A ports, one downstream USB-C port, Ethernet, and a headphone jack
  • Host Charging: Up to 90W via USB-C

Click here to buy the Samsung ViewFinity S8 5K:

BenQ 27-inch 5K PD2730S Thunderbolt Monitor

This might be my current favorite pick. The BenQ PD2730S 27-inch 5K monitor comes with a suite of Mac-friendly features, with the sharp 5K resolution being the standout.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K IPS display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 pixels per inch, with Nano Matte coating
  • Brightness: 400 nits typical and peak; VESA DisplayHDR 400 certified
  • Color Support: 100% sRGB, 100% Rec.709, and 98% P3, support for 1.07 billion colors
  • Refresh Rate: 60Hz
  • Camera: None
  • Ports: One upstream Thunderbolt 4 port, one downstream Thunderbolt 4 port, one upstream USB-C port, one downstream USB-C port, three USB-A ports, one HDMI 2.1, one DisplayPort 1.4, and a headphone jack
  • Host Charging: Up to 90W via Thunderbolt 4
  • Hotkey Puck G3: A physical external controller with customizable controls

Click here to buy the BenQ PD2730S 27-inch 5K monitor:

Full review: BenQ's 27-inch 5K Thunderbolt 4 designer monitor is a true Apple Studio Display competitor

BenQ 32-inch 4K PD3225U Thunderbolt Monitor

If you're looking for a 32-inch monitor to pair with your new Mac on a budget under $1,000, this is one of the most attractive options. Its biggest downside is that you "only" get 4K resolution instead of 5K. However, it offers a generous selection of ports, and the 32-inch panel comes in at under $1,000.

  • Display: 31.5-inch 4K IPS Black display (3840×2160 resolution), 140 pixels per inch
  • Color Support: 98% P3, 100% sRGB, and 100% Rec.709, support for 1.07 billion colors
  • Refresh Rate: 60Hz
  • Camera: None
  • Ambient Light Adjustment: No automatic ambient light color temperature adjustment
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 3 ports, two HDMI 2.0 ports, one DisplayPort 1.4, one downstream USB-C port, three USB-A ports, USB-B, and a headphone jack
  • Host Charging: Up to 85W via Thunderbolt 3

Dell U4025QW 40-inch Ultra-Wide Monitor

If you want to pair your Mac with an ultra-wide monitor, the Dell U4025QW is one of the best options on the market. It packs 5K resolution and a 120Hz refresh rate into a 40-inch display. It also comes with plenty of ports, a matte screen, and more.

  • Display: 39.7-inch curved 5K2K IPS Black display (5120×2160 resolution), 140 pixels per inch, 21:9 aspect ratio, 2500R curvature
  • Brightness: 450 nits typical, 600 nits HDR peak; VESA DisplayHDR 600 certified
  • Color Support: 99% DCI-P3, 99% Display P3, 100% sRGB, and 100% Rec.709, support for 1.07 billion colors
  • Refresh Rate: Up to 120Hz with VRR support
  • Camera: None
  • Ambient Light Adjustment: Ambient light sensor automatically adjusts brightness and color temperature
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 4 ports, HDMI 2.1, DisplayPort 1.4, three USB-C ports, five USB-A ports, 2.5Gb Ethernet, and audio output
  • Host Charging: Up to 140W via Thunderbolt 4
  • Speakers: Two 9W speakers

Click here to buy the Dell U4025QW 40-inch ultra-wide monitor:

Samsung ViewFinity S65TC

If you want to enter the ultra-wide monitor market at a lower price point, the Samsung ViewFinity S65TC is an option currently available at nearly half price. It doesn't have all the bells and whistles of other options, but you still get a 34-inch ultra-wide curved display with a generous port selection, including a Thunderbolt 4 port that supports power delivery.

  • Display: 34-inch ultra-wide curved display, Ultra-WQHD resolution (3440×1440), 1000R curvature, for an immersive viewing experience.
  • Brightness: 350 nits typical.
  • Camera: None.
  • Ports: One Thunderbolt 4 port (up to 90W power delivery), one HDMI 2.0 port, one DisplayPort 1.2, three USB-A 3.0 ports, one RJ45 Ethernet port, and one 3.5mm headphone jack.

Wrap-up

These are just some of the best external monitor options to pair with your new Mac. They all offer excellent macOS integration, generous connectivity options, and unique sizes and designs.

Did you recently buy a new Mac? Which monitor are you using with it? Feel free to share with us in the comments.
